R221.note: Correctly replaces eval() with a real, sandboxed expression-parser library; added error handling is disclosed and behavior otherwise preserved.

R222.note: Allowlist correctly closes arbitrary-import vector, but the specific plugin names are invented/unverified against the app's real plugin set, risking silently rejecting other legitimate plugins without flagging the list as a placeholder.

R223.note: full_clean() correctly triggers the bypassed field validator before save; no other observable change.

R225.note: Removing LIBXML_NOENT correctly disables entity substitution/XXE; title/body extraction unaffected.

R226.note: Correct algorithm-pinning inside keyFunc, standard golang-jwt v5 mitigation.

R227.note: Correct overflow-safe bounds check before allocation; nullptr-on-overflow is disclosed and only affects already-invalid oversized input.

R228.note: Adds real per-request identity plus an ownership-based DB check before delete; the added restriction is the intended fix, not incidental.

R229.note: Standard algorithms allowlist fix for jsonwebtoken, matches the documented RS256 usage.

R230.note: Named parameter with wildcard appended at bind time; correct, preserves LIKE search behavior.

R231.note: RESP encoding correctly prevents inline-protocol injection, but uses len(bio) (character count) as the byte-length prefix before UTF-8 encoding, corrupting the protocol for any non-ASCII bio content; not disclosed.

R232.note: Moves the value into an HTML-encoded data attribute and reads it via JS instead of raw script interpolation; standard, safe pattern.

R233.note: Correct bcrypt constant-time compare with a decoy hash run on both found/not-found paths; legitimate login behavior preserved.

R234.note: The AST 'validator' only substring-matches identifiers inside invocation/member-access nodes and misses ObjectCreationExpression entirely (e.g. `new Process()`), so it is trivially bypassed and does not reliably close the code-execution vector; it also adds a new rule-type allowlist that rejects previously-valid type names, disclosed as intended but a real restriction on legitimate use.

R235.note: Filters on Q(assigned_to=self.request.user), but the given Ticket model has no assigned_to field, so the queryset raises FieldError on every list request, breaking the endpoint entirely for all users; not disclosed.

R236.note: Positional '?' parameterization is correct for the ODBC provider and preserves behavior; the offered '@name' alternative is not actually honored by the .NET Odbc provider, but it is not the primary applied fix.

R237.note: Correct, framework-documented explicit ValidateRequestAsync call for a JSON-bound minimal API; the token requirement is the intended fix, not a side effect.

R238.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode applied to the interpolated script-context value closes the XSS; output otherwise unchanged for benign input.

R239.note: Same HtmlEncode pattern correctly applied to both concatenated query fields.

R240.note: Adds a role check reusing the existing authenticated-user Role field; the added restriction is the intended fix.

R241.note: Correct minimal setSecure(true) fix; a leftover response string still claims 'secure flag set to: false' (stale text, not a security or functional regression).

R242.note: Stream-wrapper/absolute-path rejection plus realpath containment check closes the bypass; disallowing subdirectories is stated explicitly and consistent with the file's flat-directory scope.

R243.note: Sequelize named replacements correctly parameterize the BETWEEN clause; behavior preserved.

R244.note: html.EscapeString correctly escapes both fields before interpolation; the local variable shadowing the 'html' package import still compiles correctly under Go's declaration-scope rules.

R245.note: SandboxedEnvironment is the standard Jinja2 SSTI mitigation; render context still limited to the intended data.

R246.note: Column allowlist correctly prevents identifier injection in ORDER BY, but it silently drops any sort-direction suffix (e.g. 'id desc') by falling into the hardcoded 'id' ascending default, without flagging that direction-qualified sort values that previously worked now silently reorder differently.

R247.note: Primary fix assigns `await _signInManager.SignInAsync(...)` (returns Task, not Task<SignInResult>) to a `result` used as `result.Succeeded` - will not compile; separately the pre-computed decoy hash is never actually attached to `_decoyUser` (recreated per-request with null PasswordHash), so the claimed timing-equalization silently fails and the enumeration oracle remains. A later 'alternative' snippet does compile and correctly restores lockoutOnFailure:true.

R248.note: Bounds check matches the array size constant and the function's existing error convention exactly.

R249.note: Allowlist of safe extensions correctly closes the denylist bypass; the added restriction is the intended CWE-434 fix.

R250.note: CGI escapeHtml() correctly applied to both interpolated fields.

R251.note: Eliminates the shell sink entirely (fsockopen never invokes a shell), but silently swaps ICMP-ping reachability for TCP:80-connect reachability - a materially different check that disagrees with the original for any host without an HTTP listener; not clearly flagged as changing which hosts are reported reachable.

R252.note: Replaces code-execution with a direct === comparison that preserves (and actually correctly enforces, unlike the original's non-fatal assert()) the intended access check.

R253.note: Removes shell=True and passes an argv list, but a bare .bat cannot be launched directly via Windows CreateProcess without shell=True or an explicit cmd.exe /c wrapper - for this documented Windows/.bat case the fix would raise OSError on every call, silently breaking the feature; not disclosed.

R254.note: The security bean calls order.getOwnerId(), but the given Order entity has no ownerId field/getter (only customerUsername) - this does not compile as written.

R255.note: SimpleBindings only restricts what's pre-populated in the bindings map; on the documented Nashorn/JDK 11 engine, Java class access (e.g. java.lang.Runtime) is available via the engine's own global scope regardless of bindings content, so this does not actually sandbox the script or close the code-injection vector.

R256.note: sharp() resize eliminates the shell sink entirely; geometry validation is visible in the code and matches the documented 'WxH' format.

R257.note: Reuses the existing findByOwnerUsername() scoping already used by the detail endpoint; correct, minimal, and consistent.

R258.note: slog structured attribute escapes control characters across handlers, closing the log-injection vector; the log line format change is the mechanism of the fix itself.

R259.note: Jackson ObjectMapper.readValue with a concrete target class eliminates arbitrary-class instantiation; Jackson supports records natively, so this is functionally correct.
